ns2:section.sectionText: In this course students explore how a range of regulatory agencies invoke international institutions in the governance of urban conflicts. Specifically, we will study and map how inhabitants of specific cities use international human rights regimes to claim individual and collective claims for urban citizenship and rights to the city. Learning objectives include: understanding the history and current role of international humanitarian institutions in urban governance of cities; identification of key local and trans-local actors claiming citizenship; evaluation of the legitimacy of competing citizenship claims, and; creation of a visually compelling story map argument of a specific case study in a city of the global south.
